book_title:
The First Epistle of S. Paul
to Timothee.

intros.title: THE ARGUMENT OF THE FIRST EPISTLE OF S. PAUL TO TIMOTHEE.
intros.text:
AFTER the Epistles to the Churches, now follow his Epistles to particular persons, as to Timothee, to Titus, who were Bishops; and to Philemon.
Of Timothee we read Act. 16. how S. Paul in his visitation took him in his train at Lystra, circumciding him before, because of the Jews. He was then a Disciple, that is to say, a Christian man. Afterward the Apostle gave him holy Orders, and consecrated him Bishop, as he testifieth in both these Epistles unto him. 1. Tim. 4. v. 14. and 2. Tim. 1. v. 6.
He writeth therefore unto him as to a Bishop, and himself expresseth the scope of his first Epistle, saying: These things I write to thee, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to converse in the ◦ House of God, which is the Church. And so he instructeth him (and in him, all Bishops) how to govern both himself, & others. And touching himself, to be an example & a spectacle to all sorts, in all virtue. As touching others, to prohibit all such as go about to preach otherwise than the Catholic Church hath received, and to inculcate to the people the Catholic faith: to preach unto young and old, men and women: to servants, to the rich, to every sort conveniently. With what circumspection to give orders, & to what persons: for whom to pray: whom to admit to the vow of widowhood &c. This Epistle was written, as it seemeth, after his first imprisonment in Rome, when he was dismissed and set at liberty. And thereupon it is, that he might say here, I hope to come to thee [1] quickly. to wit unto Ephesus, where he had desired him to remain. Although in his voyage to [2] Hierusalem, before his being at Rome, he said at Miletum to the Clergy of Ephesus, upon probable fear: And now behold I know, that you shall no more see my face. Where it was written, it is uncertain: though it be commonly said, at Laodicia. Which seemeth not, because it is like he was never there, as may be gathered by the Epistle to the Colossians , written ◦ at Rome in his last trouble, when he was put to death.

verses.text: <sc>PAVL</sc> an Apostle of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ according to the commandement of God our sauiour, and of Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> our hope:
to Timothee his beloued sonne in the faith. Grace, mercie, and peace from God the father, and from Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord.
As I desired thee to remaine at Ephesus vvhen I vvent into Macedonia, that thou shouldest denounce to certaine not to teache othervvise,
nor to attend to fables and genealogies hauing no ende: vvhich minister questions rather then the edifying of God vvhich is in faith.
But the ende of the precept is charitie from a pure hart, and <na>[1]</na> a good conscience, and a faith not feined.

notes.text: ∷ S. Augustine saith, He that list to haue the hope of heauē let him looke that he haue a good cōsciēce. to haue a good conscience, let him beleeue & vvorke vvel. for that he beleueth, he hath of faith: that he vvorketh, he hath of charitie. Præfat. in Psa. 31.

verses.text: From the vvhich things certaine straying, are turned into <na>[1]</na> vaine talke,

notes.text: c ματαιολογίαν,

verses.text: desirous to be doctors of the Lavv, not vnderstanding neither vvhat things they speake, nor of vvhat they affirme.
But vve knovv that <cr>[1]</cr> the Lavv is good, if a man vse it lavvfully:

knovving this that the Lavv is not made to the iust man, but to the vniust and disobedient, to the impious and sinners, to the vvicked and contaminate, to killers of fathers and killers of mothers, to murderers,
to fornicatours, to lyers vvith man-kinde, to man-stealers, to liers, to periured persons, and vvhat other thing soeuer is contrarie to sound doctrine,
vvhich is according to the Gospel of the glorie of the blessed God, vvhich is committed to me.
I giue him thankes vvhich hath strengthened me, Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> our Lord, because he hath esteemed me faithful, putting me in the ministerie.
vvho before vvas blasphemous and a persecutor & contumelious. but I obteined the mercie of God, because I did it being ignorant in incredulitie.
And the grace of our Lord ouer-abounded vvith faith and loue, vvhich is in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
A faithful saying, & vvorthie of al acceptatiō, that Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> came into this vvorld <cr>[1]</cr> to saue sinners, of vvhom I am the cheefe.
But therfore haue I obtained mercie: that in me first of al Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> might shevv al patience, <na>[1]</na> to the information of them that shal beleeue on him vnto life euerlasting.

notes.text: c πρὸς ὑποτύπωσιν

verses.text: And to the king of the vvorldes, immortal, inuisible, onely God, honour & glorie for euer and euer. Amen.
This precept I commend to thee ô Timothee: according to the prophecies going before <na>[1]</na> on thee, that thou vvarre in them a good vvarfare,

notes.text: c ἐπί σε

verses.text: hauing faith and a good conscience, <na>[1]</na> vvhich certaine repelling, haue made shipvvracke about the faith.

notes.text: Evil life and no good conscience is often the cause that men fall to Heresy from the faith of the Catholic Church. Again, this plainly reproveth the heretics' false doctrine, saying, that no man can fall from the faith that he once truly had.

verses.text: Of vvhom is Hymenæus & Alexander: vvhom I haue deliuered to Satan, that they may learne not to blaspheme.

chapters.summary: He recommendeth vnto him, to inhibite certaine Ievves vvho iangled of the Lavv as though it vvere contrarie to his preaching. 11 Against vvhom he auoucheth his ministerie, though he acknovvledge his vnvvorthines.

verses.text: I Desire therfore first of al things that obsecrations, praiers, postulations, thankesgeuings be made for al men,
<na>[1]</na> for kings and al that are in preeminence: that vve may leade a quiet and a peaceable life in al pietie and chastitie.

notes.text: Euen for heathen kings & Emperours by vvhom the Church suffereth persecution: much more for al faithful Princes & powers, and people both spiritual and temporal, for vvhom as members of Christes body, and therfore ioyning in praier & oblation vvith the ministers of the Church, the Priestes more properly and particularly offer the holy Sacrifice. See S. Augustine de orig. animæ li. 1. c. 9.

verses.text: For this is good and acceptable before our Sauiour God,
vvho vvill al men to be saued, and to come to the knovvledge of the truth,
For there is one God, one also mediatour of God and men, man Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>:
vvho gaue himself a redemption for al, <na>[1]</na> <alt>vvhose testimonie</alt> in due times is confirmed: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: The prayers & petitions in the Mass,

verses.text: <cr>[1]</cr> vvherein I am appointed a preacher & an Apostle (I say the truth, I lie not) doctor of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
I vvil therfore that men pray in euery place: lifting vp pure handes, vvithout anger and altercation.
In like maner <cr>[1]</cr> vvomen also in comely attire: vvith demurenesse and sobrietie adorning them selues, not in plaited heare, or gold, or pretious stones, or gorgeous apparel,
but that vvhich becommeth vvomen professing pietie by good vvorkes.
Let a vvoman learne in silence, vvith al subiection.
But <cr>[1]</cr> to teach I permit not vnto a vvoman, nor to haue dominion ouer the man: but to be in silence.
For <cr>[1]</cr> Adam vvas formed first: then Eue.
and Adam vvas not seduced: but the vvoman being seduced, vvas in preuarication.
Yet she shal be saued by generation of children: if <na>[1]</na> <alt>'they</alt>' continue in faith & loue and sanctification vvith sobrietie.

notes.text: 'she

chapters.summary: By his Apostolike authoritie he appointeth publike praiers to be made for al mē vvithout exception. 8 also men to pray in al places: 9 and vvomen also in semely attire, 11 to learne of men, and not to be teachers in any vvise, but to seeke saluation, by that vvhich to them belongeth.

verses.text: A Faithful saying. If a man desire a Bishops office, he desireth a good vvorke.
<cr>[1]</cr> It behoueth therfore a Bishop to be irreprehensible, the husband of one vvife, sobre, vvise, comely, chast, a man of hospitalitie, a teacher,
not giuen to vvine, no fighter, but modest, no quareler, not couetous,
vvel ruling his ovvne house, <na>[1]</na> hauing his children subiect vvith al chastitie.

notes.text: c He saith, having children, not, getting children. S. Ambr. Ep. 82.

verses.text: But if a man knovv not to rule his ovvne house: hovv shal he haue care of the Church of God?
Not <na>[1]</na> <na>[2]</na> a neophyte: lest puffed into pride, he fall into the iudgment of the Deuil.

notes.text: b Neophytus is he that vvas lately christened or nevvely planted in the mystical body of Christ.
b νεόφυτον

verses.text: And he must haue also good testimonie of them that are vvithout: that he fall not into reproch and the snare of the Deuil.
Deacons in like maner <na>[1]</na> cchast, not double-tonged, not giuen to much vvine, not folovvers of filthie lucre:

notes.text: c σεμνοὺς

verses.text: hauing the mysterie of faith in a pure conscience.
And let these also be proued first: & so let them minister, hauing no crime.
The vvomen in like maner chast, not detracting, sober, faithful in al things.
Let deacons be the husbandes of one vvife: vvhich rule vvel their children, & their houses.
For they that haue ministred vvel, shal purchase to them selues a good degree, and much confidence in the faith vvhich is in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
These things I vvrite to thee, hoping that I shal come to thee quickly.
but if I tary long, that thou maiest knovv hovv thou oughtest to conuerse in the house of God, vvhich is the <sc>CHVRCH</sc> of the liuing God, the piller and ground of truth.

And manifestly it is a great sacrament of pietie, vvhich vvas manifested in flesh, vvas iustified in spirit, appeared to Angels, hath beene preached to gentils, is beleeued in the vvorld, is assumpted in glorie.

chapters.summary: Of vvhat qualitie they must be, vvhom he ordaineth Bishops, 8 and Deacons. 14 and the cause of his vvriting to be, the excellencie of the Catholike Church, and of Christ, vvho is the obiect of our religion.

verses.text: <sc>AND</sc> <cr>[1]</cr> the Spirit manifestly saith that in the last times certain shal depart from the faith attending to spirites of errour, and doctrines of diuels,
speaking lies in hypocrisie, and hauing their conscience seared,
forbidding to marie, to abstaine from meates vvhich God created to receaue vvith thankes-giuing for the faithful, and them that haue knovven the truth.
For <na>[1]</na> euery creature of God is good, and nothing to be reiected that is receiued vvith thankes-giuing.

notes.text: vve see plainely by these vvordes such abstinence only to be disalovved as condemneth the creatures of God to be naught by nature & creation.

verses.text: For it is sanctified by the vvord of God and praier.

These things proposing to the brethren, thou shalt <na>[1]</na> <na>[2]</na> be a good minister of Christ IESVS, nourished in the vvordes of the faith and the good doctrine vvhich thou hast attained vnto.

notes.text: All Heretics are apostates from the faith.
ἀποστήσονται

verses.text: But folish and old vviues fables auoid: and exercise thy self to pietie.
<cr>[1]</cr> For <na>[2]</na> corporal exercise is profitable to litle: but pietie is profitable to al things: hauing promisse of the life that novv is, and of that to come.

notes.text: Some (saith S. Chrysost.) expound this of fasting, but they are deceiued. for fasting is a spiritual exercise. See a goodly commentarie of these vvordes in S. August. li. de mor. Eccl. Cath. c. 33. · 1. Tim. 1, 4. Tit. 3, 9.

verses.text: A faithful saying and vvorthie of al acceptation.
For to this purpose vve labour and are reuiled, because vve hope in the liuing God vvhich is the Sauiour of al men, especially of the faithful.
Commaund these things and teach.
Let no man contemne thy youth: but be an example of the faithful, in vvord, in conuersation, in charitie, in faith, in chastitie.
Til I come, attend vnto reading, exhortation, <na>[1]</na> doctrine.

notes.text: and

verses.text: Neglect not the grace that is in thee: vvhich is giuen thee by prophecie, vvith imposition of the handes of priesthod.
These things doe thou meditate, be in these things: that thy profiting may be manifest to al.
Attend to thy self, and to doctrine: be earnest in them. For, this doing, thou shalt saue both thy self and them that heare thee.

chapters.summary: He prophecieth that certaine should depart from the Catholike faith, vvilling Timothee therfore to inculcate to the people those articles of the said faith. 7 Item to exercise him self in spiritual exercise, 12 to gette authoritie by example of good life, 13 to studie, to teach, to increase in the grace giuen him by holy orders.

verses.text: A Seniour rebuke not: but beseeche as a father: yong men, as brethren:
old vvomen, as mothers: yong vvomen, as sisters, in al chastitie.
<na>[1]</na> Honour vvidovves: vvhich are vvidovves in deede.

notes.text: The Epistle upon S. Monica's day. May. 4. And for holy widows.

verses.text: But if any vvidovv haue children or nephevves: let her learne first to rule her ovvne house, and to render mutual dutie to her parents. for this is acceptable before God.
But she that is a vvidovv in deede and desolate: let her hope in God, and continue in obsecrations & <na>[1]</na> praiers night and day.

notes.text: Because of this continual praier vvhich standeth not vvith coniugal & carnal actes of matrimonie ( as the Apostle signifieth 1 Cor. 7, 5 ) therfore vvere these vvidovves to liue in the state of perpetual continencie.

verses.text: For she that is in deliciousenes, liuing is dead.
And this commaund that they be blamlesse.
But if any man haue not care of his ovvne, and especially of his domesticals, he hath denied the faith, and is vvorse then an infidel.
Let a vvidovv be chosen of no lesse thē three score yeres, vvhich hath been the vvife of one husband,

hauing testimonie in good vvorkes, if she haue brought vp her children, if she haue receiued to harbour, if she haue vvashed the Saincts feete, if she haue ministred to them that suffer tribulation, if she haue folovved euery good vvorke. ⊢
But the yonger vvidovves auoid. For vvhen they shal be vvanton in Christ, they vvil marie:
hauing damnation, because they haue made void their first faith.
and vvithal idle also they learne to goe about from house to house: not only idle, but also ful of vvordes and curious, speaking things vvhich they ought not.
I vvil therfore the yonger to marie, to bring forth children, to be housevviues: to giue no occasion to the aduersarie for to speake euil.
For novv certaine are turned backe after Satan.
If any faithful man haue vvidovves, let him minister to them, and let not the Church be burdened: that there may be sufficient for them that are vvidovves in deede.
The priestes that rule vvel, let them be esteemed <na>[1]</na> vvorthie of double honour: especially they that labour in the vvord and doctrine.

notes.text: c Double honour and liuelihod due to good Priestes.

verses.text: For the Scripture saith: [1] Thou shalt not moosel the mouth to the oxe that treadeth out the corne and, The vvorke man is vvorthie of his hire.
<na>[1]</na> Against a priest receiue not accusation: but vnder tvvo or three vvitnesses.

notes.text: Here the Apostle vvil not haue euery light felovv to be heard against a priest. So S. Augustin for the like reuerence of priesthod, admonisheth Pācarius that in no vvise he admitte any testimonies or accusations of Heretikes against a Catholike priest. ep. 212.

verses.text: Them that sinne, reproue before al: that the rest also may haue feare.
I testifie before God and Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, and the elect Angels, that thou keepe these things vvithout preiudice, doing nothing by declining to the one part.
Impose hādes on no man <na>[1]</na> lightly, neither do thou communicate vvith other mens sinnes. Keepe thy self chast.

notes.text: Bishops must haue great care that they giue not orders to any that is not vvel tried for his faith, learning, and good behauiour.

verses.text: Drinke not yet vvater: but vse a litle vvine for thy stomake, and thy often infirmities.
Certaine mens sinnes be manifest, going before to iudgement: and <na>[1]</na> certaine men they folovv.

notes.text: also

verses.text: In like maner also good deedes be manifest, & they that are othervvise, can not be hidde.

chapters.summary: Hovv to behaue him self tovvardes yong and old. 3 to bestovv the Churches oblations vpon the needy vvidovves. 9 and not to admitte the said Churches vvidovves vnder threescore yeres old. 17 In distribution to respect vvel the Priests that are painful. 19 and hovv in his Consistorie to heare accusations against Priests. 22 to be straite in examining before he giue Orders. to be chast, and to remitte somevvhat of his drinking vvater.

verses.text: <sc>WHOSOEVER</sc> are seruantes vnder yoke, let them counte their maisters vvorthie of al honour: lest the name of our Lord and his doctrine be blasphemed.

But they that haue faithful maisters, let them not contemne them because they are brethren, but serue the rather, because they be faithful and beloued, vvhich are partakers of the benefite. These things teache and exhort.
If any man <na>[1]</na><na>[2]</na> teach othervvise, and consent not to the sound vvordes of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ, and to that doctrine vvhich is according to pietie:

notes.text: See the annotation before cap. 1, 3. 4.
ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖ

verses.text: he is proude, knovving nothing, but languishing about questions and strife of vvordes: of vvhich rise enuies, contentions, blasphemies, euil suspicions,
conflictes of men corrupted in their minde, and that are depriued of the truth, that esteeme gaine to be pietie.
But <na>[1]</na> bpietie vvith sufficiencie is great gaine.

notes.text: b The Epistle for S. Alexius, Iul. 17.

verses.text: For vve <cr>[1]</cr> brought nothing into this vvorld: doubtlesse, neither can vve take avvay any thing.
But <cr>[1]</cr> hauing foode, and vvhervvith to be couered, vvith these vve are content.
For they that vvil be made riche, fall into tentation & the snare of the deuil, & many desires vnprofitable and hurteful, vvhich drovvne men into destruction and perdition.
For the roote of al euils is couetousenes: <na>[1]</na> vvhich certaine desiring haue erred from the faith, and haue intangled them selues in many sorovves.

notes.text: As in the 1. chap. lacke of faith and good conscience, so here couetousnes or desire of these temporal things, & in the end of this chap. presumption and boasting of knovvledge, are causes of falling from the faith: heresie often being the punishmēt of former sinnes.

verses.text: But thou, ô man of God, flee these things: and <na>[1]</na> pursue iustice, pietie, faith, charitie, patience, mildenes.

notes.text: b The Epistle for S. Timothee, Ian. 24.

verses.text: Fight the good fight of faith: apprehend eternal life, ⊢ vvherein thou art called and hast confessed a good confession before many vvitnesses.
I commaund thee before God vvho quickeneth al things, and Chirst <sc>IESVS</sc> vvho <cr>[1]</cr> gaue testimonie vnder Pontius Pilate a good confession:
that thou keepe the commaundement vvithout spotte, blamelesse vnto the comming of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
vvhich in due times the Blessed & onely Mightie vvil shevv, the <cr>[1]</cr> King of kings and Lord of lordes,
vvho only hath immortalitie, and inhabiteth light not accessible, <cr>[1]</cr> vvhom no man hath seen, yea neither can see, to vvhom be honour and empire euerlasting. Amen. ⊢
Commaund the riche of this vvorld not to be high minded, nor to trust in the vncertaintie of riches, but in the liuing God (vvho giueth vs al things aboundantly to enioy)
to doe vvel, to become riche in good vvorkes, to giue easily, to communicate,
to heape vnto them selues a good <na>[1]</na> foūdation for the time to come, that they may apprehend the true life.

notes.text: Almes deedes and good vvorkes laide for a foundatiō and ground to attaine euerlasting life. So say the doctors vpō this place.

verses.text: O Timothee, keepe the depositum, auoiding the profane [1] cnouelties of voices, & oppositions of falsely called knovvledge.

notes.text: c καινοφωνίας. S. Chrysostom.

verses.text: Vvhich certaine promising, haue erred about the faith. Grace be vvith thee. Amen.

chapters.summary: Vvhat to teach seruants. 3 If any teach against the doctrine of the Church obstinately, he doth it of pride and for lucre. 11 But the Catholike Bishop must follovv vertue, hauing his eie alvvaies to life euerlasting and to the comming of Christ. 17 Vvhat to commaund the riche. 20 Finally, to keepe most carefully the Catholike Churches doctrine, vvithout mutation.
